power.title: Power Analysis Check
report: No power analyses were detected.

::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::

prereg_check.title: Preregistration Check

table.title: Comprehension-Intact Non-Updating in Blame Revision: Preregistered Secondary Reanalysis
table.research_questions:
RQ1. Among evaluators who demonstrably register an exculpatory manipulation (both manipulation checks passed, plausibility affirmed), does a non-updating response profile occur at or above the smallest prevalence of interest (10 per cent)?

RQ2. Is the between-person distribution of blame updating in this paradigm better described by a latent mixture containing a discrete near-zero updating class than by a single population with continuously distributed heterogeneity?

Statistical framework: frequentist interval-based decision rules (Wilson intervals, conjunctive mixture-selection rules), with Bayesian beta-binomial posterior summaries reported alongside every prevalence verdict as co-primary estimation; the Bayesian summaries never alter a verdict. Full specification: Preregistration_v1.0.pdf and Analysis_Plan_Technical_v1.0.md, uploaded to the registered project and frozen with this registration. H1 (existence and prevalence; primary; directional; Theisen & Andow, 2025, Experiment 2). Among participants who, on their fulfilled-obligations/biased-evidence trial, (a) passed both manipulation checks under the original authors' criterion (responses strictly on the correct side of the scale midpoint for both checks), (b) rated the scenario above the scale midpoint on the plausibility check (> 50), and (c) gave a pre-information act-blameworthiness composite of at least 20, the proportion showing no meaningful reduction in act blameworthiness (change score > -5, using the original authors' own 5-point smallest meaningful blame reduction) is at least 10 per cent (the smallest prevalence of interest, SPI; provenance and justification in Preregistration Section 7.1).

H2 (discrete non-updating component; Theisen & Andow, 2025, Experiment 2). The between-person distribution of blame updating across the four moral-ignorance trials is better described by a latent-mixture model containing a near-zero updating class (model-implied mean change in the fulfilled/biased condition within [-5, +5]) than by a single-population linear mixed model with continuously distributed heterogeneity, under fixed model-selection rules (delta-BIC >= 6 AND parametric bootstrap LRT p < .01 with B = 500 AND smallest class >= 5 per cent AND no boundary solution). H2 does not establish psychological kinds by itself; it tests whether this dataset is better represented by a near-zero latent component than by continuous heterogeneity under severe preregistered rules.

No third confirmatory hypothesis is registered. An earlier internal draft carried a gated hypothesis for Landy and Perry (2024); reading their published Method before registration settled the gate negatively (no within-person updating structure, no mitigating information, no comprehension checks), so it was withdrawn before registration and before any data access.

S1 (secondary; dissociation-consistent subset). Among the H1 qualifying set, the proportion showing no meaningful blame reduction AND rating the agent's belief blameworthiness at or below the scale midpoint (composite <= 50) is at least 5 per cent.

S2 (secondary; comprehension-registration guard). The "comprehension-intact" qualifier attached to any H1 signal is retained only if non-updaters show no detectable registration deficit relative to updaters on the two manipulation checks, each expressed as condition-consistent registration strength (on the FB trial: obligations strength = raw obligations-check score; evidence strength = 100 minus raw evidence-check score). Conjunctive per check: (a) one-sided Welch deficit test non-significant at alpha = .05, and (b) observed standardised deficit < 0.4 pooled SD. If either check fails either condition, the qualifier is withdrawn and the H1 verdict is capped at "non-updating present but not demonstrably comprehension-intact". Full TOST equivalence tests (bounds +/- 0.4 SD) are additionally reported and, if passed on both checks, license the stronger wording "statistically equivalent registration".

Complete verbatim hypotheses, decision rules, exclusions, robustness set, and the binding results-interpretation table are in Preregistration_v1.0.pdf and Analysis_Plan_Technical_v1.0.md, frozen with this registration.
table.datasets_used:
Primary and sole confirmatory dataset: Theisen, M., & Andow, J. (2025). The exculpatory potential of moral ignorance: Evidence from a blame-updating paradigm. Synthese, 207, 36. Within-person blame-updating experiments (total N = 500; Exp 1 n = 251, Exp 2 n = 249; German-language, Prolific, DACH region). Participants rated act blameworthiness before and after learning the agent was morally ignorant, with exculpatory strength manipulated in a 2x2 within-person design (procedural obligations fulfilled/violated x moral evidence biased/unbiased), plus a control trial. CONFIRMATORY SUBSET: Experiment 2 only (n = 249), the only experiment including manipulation checks for both factors, a plausibility check, and belief-blameworthiness measures; the H1/S1/S2 qualifying set is the fulfilled-obligations/biased-evidence trial of participants passing both checks with plausibility > 50 and pre-blame >= 20 (expected |Q| approximately 55-65). Experiment 1 is exploratory only (no manipulation checks; recurrence of non-updating, never comprehension-intactness).

Secondary, exploratory-descriptive only: Landy, J. F., & Perry, A. D. (2024). Forming evaluations of moral character. Cognitive Science, 48(4), e13443. Four preregistered studies (final n approximately 680). No within-person updating structure, no mitigating information, no comprehension checks (established from the published Method before registration); contributes the published linear-averaging anchor plus one pre-declared exploratory descriptive (E4), supplement only.
table.data_access: No access restrictions: both datasets are on public OSF projects under open licences. CRITICAL PROVENANCE STATEMENT: as of this registration, NO data file, analysis script, codebook file, or supplementary file from either source project has been downloaded, opened, previewed, or otherwise inspected by the author or by any automated or AI agent acting on the author's behalf. For Landy and Perry, file and folder names on the OSF project page were viewed (contents were not); the Theisen and Andow OSF project has not been visited at all. First data contact will occur only after this registration is public, and every file will be logged (source, URL, file id, method, downloader, local path, SHA-256, timestamp, and OSF file version and date-modified where visible) in the project's access log, published with the results.
table.data_identifiers: Theisen & Andow (2025): article DOI 10.1007/s11229-025-05405-9; data/materials OSF DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/9BY25 (project not yet visited). Landy & Perry (2024): article DOI 10.1111/cogs.13443; data and scripts at https://osf.io/fj6wg (file names viewed, contents not opened).
table.access_date: Not yet accessed. No data have been downloaded or viewed as of registration (11 July 2026). First access will occur only after this registration is public and timestamped; the exact download date and per-file SHA-256 checksums will be recorded in the project's access log and published with the results.
table.data_collection_procedures: Both data collections are documented in the published, peer-reviewed articles cited above (methods, materials, exclusion rules, and preregistrations for Landy & Perry). Theisen & Andow (2025): online experiments on Prolific, German-language, DACH region (Exp 1 collected 19 September 2023; Exp 2 collected 27-28 August 2025, per the published article); convenience samples, so prevalence estimates are paradigm- and sample-specific and are reported as such. Landy & Perry (2024): four preregistered online studies. Representativeness caveat: both are online convenience samples; no weights exist or will be constructed; all claims are bounded to these paradigms (Preregistration Section 3.4).
table.codebook: No codebook has been opened before registration (by design: the no-prior-access protocol covers codebook files). Variable identification proceeds from the published articles' verbatim item wordings and method descriptions alone; the frozen variable-mapping protocol (Preregistration Section 4.5) governs mapping published wordings to archived variable names at first data contact, with any conflict between the published rule and the archived codebook resolved in favour of the published rule and reported as a deviation. The most relevant documentation is the Method sections of the two published articles.
table.manipulated_variables: Manipulated in the original study (Theisen & Andow, 2025, Exp 2; within-person 2x2 plus control): (1) procedural obligations regarding moral knowledge (fulfilled vs violated); (2) moral evidence available to the agent (biased vs unbiased); one trial per condition per participant. The confirmatory qualifying cell is fulfilled-obligations/biased-evidence (FB), the strongest exculpatory combination. MANIPULATION-CHECK DECISION RULE (fixed): pass requires responses strictly on the condition-consistent side of the scale midpoint on BOTH checks (original authors' criterion; midpoint-exact = fail). H1/S1/S2 are computed only within the qualifying set Q (both checks passed AND plausibility > 50 AND pre-information blame composite >= 20). Feasibility gate: if |Q| < 40, H1 and S1 are reported descriptively and labelled uninterpretable for the smallest-prevalence test; no prevalence verdict is issued.
table.measured_variables: PRIMARY OUTCOME: act-blameworthiness change score per ignorance trial = post-information minus pre-information composite; each composite is the mean of three 0-100 slider items (responsibility, blame, reproach) per the published method; change range -100 to +100; negative = blame reduction. Non-updating indicator (H1): change > -5 on the FB trial (original authors' 5-point smallest meaningful reduction). QUALIFICATION/GUARD VARIABLES: obligations manipulation check (0-100); moral-evidence manipulation check (0-100); plausibility check (0-100); belief-blameworthiness composite (0-100; S1 threshold <= 50). S2 registration-strength transforms: obligations strength = raw obligations score; evidence strength = 100 minus raw evidence score (FB cell; higher always = stronger condition-consistent registration). H2 input: the person-level vector of four ignorance-trial change scores [FB, FU, VB, VU]. DESCRIPTIVE PROFILE TAXONOMY (descriptive only, no confirmatory claims): Updater (change_FB <= -5); Operational non-updater (change_FB > -5); Dissociation-consistent non-updater (change_FB > -5 and belief blame <= 50); Principled non-excuser (change_FB > -5 and belief blame > 50); Threshold-adjacent (change_FB in [-10, 0]); Literal non-mover (exact pre/post equality on all blame items). No EFA/CFA; composites follow the published scoring exactly. All aggregation rules are fixed in the frozen pipeline (analysis_pipeline.py, SHA-256 recorded in the attached documents).
table.missing_data_handling: Missingness rates are unknown pre-registration (no data contact); the published article reports complete-case analyses after its exclusions. Rules (fixed): H1/S1/S2 use trials with complete pre and post composites on the FB trial; trials with missing pre or post composites are excluded listwise from trial-level analyses. H2 requires the complete four-trial change vector; participants with incomplete vectors are excluded from H2 only, and their number is counted and reported. No imputation is used; observed missingness will be reported descriptively alongside the confirmatory outputs. Expected qualifying set from published figures: roughly 55-65 participants (30.5 per cent of 249 pass both checks in the critical cell, before the plausibility and pre-blame floors).
table.unit_of_analysis: Unit of analysis: the participant (H1, S1, S2, E4) or the participant-level four-trial change vector after reshaping (H2 and the mixture models); participant-by-trial data are used only before reshaping. Inclusion for the confirmatory qualifying set Q (Exp 2, FB trial): both manipulation checks passed (strict midpoint rule), plausibility > 50, pre-information blame composite >= 20, complete pre/post composites, and survival of the original authors' published exclusions (applied first) plus the straightlining guard. Expected |Q| approximately 55-65; feasibility gate |Q| >= 40. H2 expected n approximately 200+ (all Exp 2 participants with complete four-vectors, before qualification filters, per the frozen rules).
table.statistical_outliers: No outlier removal, trimming, or winsorising is planned or permitted anywhere in the pipeline (fixed exclusion rule): all confirmatory measures are bounded 0-100 sliders, the change scale is bounded at [-100, +100], and extreme values on bounded scales are data, not artefacts. The straightlining guard (identical pre-information ratings across all five distinct actions with zero variance) is the only response-quality exclusion beyond the original authors' published flags, and it cannot exclude genuine non-updaters, whose pre ratings vary across actions while their change scores sit near zero. Definitive expected confirmatory sample: |Q| approximately 55-65 (gate at 40).
table.sampling_weights: Neither dataset carries sampling weights (both are online convenience samples), and no weights will be constructed or applied. All prevalence claims are explicitly paradigm- and sample-bounded; no population-representative generalisation is made.
table.prior_publication_dissemination: None. The author has never published, presented, or drafted any work based on either dataset, has never analysed any variable from either dataset, and has had no collaboration, correspondence, presentation, or peer-review contact with either author team. A related theoretical manuscript by the author (Trait Judgmentalism / Contextual Moderation Failure, submitted to New Ideas in Psychology) cites both published articles but uses no data from them; this registration is the first empirical work connected to that framework.
table.prior_knowledge: Sole author; prior knowledge derives entirely from reading the published articles and search listings, never from data. Itemised in full in Preregistration_v1.0 Section 8 (known-findings disclosure) and summarised here. Theisen & Andow (2025): the article full text as rendered from the publisher page was read on 10 July 2026, truncated within Section 6.2.1, so the closing discussion and end matter were NOT read and will not be consulted until confirmatory outputs are frozen. Known: complete method descriptions for both experiments, verbatim item wordings, the manipulation-check pass criterion, and group-level results text including exact coefficients and effect sizes, and the exploratory check-passer subset results (including that 30.5 per cent of Experiment 2 participants pass both checks in the critical cell). NOT known: any person-level value, distribution, spread, or count of non-updaters; the target estimands (person-level prevalence within the qualifying set, dissociation subset size, mixture structure) appear nowhere in the published article and are not derivable from the known group statistics. Landy & Perry (2024): article full text read, including methods, scale wordings, exclusion counts, and group-level results; OSF project page visited with file and folder NAMES viewed to two levels; no file contents, no data, no analysis scripts, no supplementary documents, no AsPredicted PDFs were opened. The Theisen & Andow OSF project was not visited at all. Web search listings naming the papers were read. No codebook from either project has been opened. AI assistance: automated retrieval of the published article pages listed above was carried out by an AI assistant (Anthropic's Claude) under the author's direction, and a second-model-family audit (OpenAI Codex) reviewed the package; no AI agent accessed either OSF data archive. The registered hypotheses' key thresholds (the 5-point non-updating threshold; the manipulation-check pass rule) are the original authors' own published choices, fixed here precisely so that no threshold is tuned to any known result.
table.statistical_tests: H1/S1 (prevalence): the observed proportion in the qualifying set Q is tested against the smallest prevalence of interest via the Wilson score interval (95 per cent); a Jeffreys Beta(0.5, 0.5) beta-binomial posterior is reported as co-primary estimation (median, 95 per cent credible interval, Pr(P >= .10), Pr(P <= .05), uniform-prior sensitivity) and never alters the verdict. H2 (mixture vs continuous heterogeneity): baseline M0 = compound-symmetry multivariate normal on the person-level four-trial change vector [FB, FU, VB, VU] (the wide-form equivalent of a random-intercept linear mixed model); MK = Gaussian mixture models with K = 2, 3 (tied/full covariance selected by BIC within K); a near-zero class is defined by model-implied FB mean change within [-5, +5]. Decision rule (conjunctive, fixed): delta-BIC >= 6 in favour of MK AND parametric bootstrap likelihood-ratio test p < .01 (B = 500) AND smallest class proportion >= 5 per cent AND no boundary solution; a K = 3 bootstrap that is attempted and unavailable (non-convergence) forces the H2 verdict to indeterminate, never a default K = 2 pass. S2 (registration guard): one-sided Welch tests on condition-consistent registration strength plus 0.4 pooled-SD deficit cap, conjunctive per check; TOST equivalence (bounds +/- 0.4 SD) reported descriptively. Everything is implemented in the frozen pipeline analysis_pipeline.py (primary registered executable; SHA-256 in the attached manifest), validated end to end on synthetic data at B = 500 before registration; analysis_skeleton.R is a non-executable rule mirror. Any analysis not specified here or in the attached documents is exploratory.
table.effect_size: Smallest prevalence of interest (SPI): 10 per cent for H1, 5 per cent for S1 (provenance in Preregistration Section 7.1: fixed pre-data, not derivable from any known group statistic, functioning as the claim-licensing threshold in the SESOI sense, Lakens et al., 2018). The theory itself predicts only prevalence > 0; no registered hypothesis requires any particular prevalence for the framework to survive. H2 smallest class proportion of interest: 5 per cent. S2 deficit cap: 0.4 pooled SD.
table.statistical_power: Stated honestly and quantified pre-registration (Technical Plan Section 10): at |Q| = 60, the design cannot sharply distinguish a true prevalence of 10 per cent from 5 per cent (signal probability approximately .03 at true P1 = .10; bound probability approximately .19 at true P1 = .05). The design separates "well above 10 per cent" from "essentially absent"; between those, the pre-licensed outcome is indeterminate wording plus the Bayesian posterior as graded evidence, estimate-first. H2 verdict-probability simulation (100 replicates per truth, full registered rule): at true prevalence 0 per cent, bound verdict 100/100 (zero false classes); at 15 per cent, signal .93. This registration accepts the indeterminate zone rather than inflating claims.
table.inference_criteria: H1: signal if the Wilson 95 per cent lower bound >= .10; bound (evidence against) if the upper bound < .10 with upper bound < .05 licensing "essentially absent"; otherwise indeterminate. One-sided in the direction of the hypothesis; the near-one-sided character of the rule is disclosed. S1: same logic against .05. H2: the conjunctive rule stated under Statistical Models, with an exhaustive four-way verdict mapping (signal / bound / indeterminate / heterogeneity-without-a-non-updating-class); disagreement between BIC and bootstrap = indeterminate, M0 retained. S2 caps the H1 wording as specified. Multiplicity: H1 and S1 are a fixed two-test family in a fixed hierarchy (S1 interpreted only within an H1-qualified set); H2 is a single model comparison; no other confirmatory tests exist, and every registered quantity has exactly one decision rule. ALL result wording is pre-licensed in a binding interpretation table (Technical Plan Section 8): signal, bound, indeterminate, and uninterpretable outcomes each carry an exact citable sentence, and claims travel to any paper only through that wording. Bayesian posteriors are reported alongside every prevalence verdict but never override the Wilson rule.
table.assumption_violation_model_non_convergen: Fixed in advance (Technical Plan Sections 5.2 and 5.4): mixture non-convergence or boundary solutions map to the indeterminate verdict, never to a fallback pass; a K = 3 bootstrap attempted and unavailable forces indeterminate. Mandatory sensitivity refits guard the H2 class against artefacts: (i) multivariate-t and skew-normal K = 1 comparators (a heavy-tail or skew model beating the mixture by BIC overturns the class as a named artefact); (ii) exact-zero inflation reassignment diagnostic (a class consisting solely of literal slider non-movement is named as such); (iii) pre-blame floor refit with covariate sensitivity. Every such overturn has pre-licensed wording. No rule may be changed post-contact; any forced deviation is reported in a mandatory Deviations section (present even if empty).
table.reliability_and_robustness_testing: Pre-specified robustness/multiverse (Technical Plan Section 7): a 108-cell prevalence multiverse crossing the non-updating threshold (> -5 registered; 0 and -10 arms), plausibility criterion (> 50 registered; >= 60 arm), pre-blame floor (>= 20 registered; >= 10 and >= 30 arms), check rule (both strict, registered; either-check arm), and control-trial adjustment (unadjusted registered; control-adjusted arm), plus an 8-cell H2 multiverse. Reported as a specification curve with the exact proportion of cells reproducing the registered verdict (no dichotomous robust/fragile label). The pipeline was validated end to end on synthetic data (six scenarios plus artefact and small-N stress cases) at the registered B = 500 under the final pipeline hash before registration; the validation outputs are attached (validation.zip).
table.exploratory_analyses: Pre-declared exploratory outputs (labelled as such in any report; no confirmatory claims): E1, the descriptive profile taxonomy within Q (updater; operational non-updater; dissociation-consistent non-updater; principled non-excuser; threshold-adjacent; literal non-mover); E2, Theisen & Andow Experiment 1 recurrence check (same paradigm, no manipulation checks, explicitly labelled "not comprehension-intact"), compared descriptively with the Experiment 2 confirmatory estimate; E3, alternative-explanations diagnostic table (failed comprehension -> S2; implausibility -> plausibility criterion; floor effects -> floor and multiverse; belief-level blame -> S1 and taxonomy; slider non-engagement -> exact-zero diagnostics; response-quality failure -> straightlining rule; arbitrary threshold -> threshold multiverse; retest drift -> control-adjusted sensitivity; continuous heterogeneity -> H2/M0); E4, one supplement-only descriptive from Landy & Perry Study 4 (single difference score; no updating interpretation). Planned figures: sample-to-Q flow diagram; FB change-score distribution in Q with the -5 threshold marked; manipulation-check scores for updaters vs non-updaters; specification curve; optional taxonomy bar chart. Reporting: one bounded paragraph in the New Ideas in Psychology manuscript using only the pre-licensed wording, plus a standalone short report (target Collabra: Psychology or Meta-Psychology), all outcomes reported with equal prominence.

Among evaluators who demonstrably register an exculpatory manipulation (both manipulation checks passed, plausibility affirmed), does a non-updating response profile occur at or above the smallest prevalence of interest (10 per cent)?

RQ2. Is the between-person distribution of blame updating in this paradigm better described by a latent mixture containing a discrete near-zero updating class than by a single population with continuously distributed heterogeneity?

Statistical framework: frequentist interval-based decision rules (Wilson intervals, conjunctive mixture-selection rules), with Bayesian beta-binomial posterior summaries reported alongside every prevalence verdict as co-primary estimation; the Bayesian summaries never alter a verdict. Full specification: Preregistration_v1.0.pdf and Analysis_Plan_Technical_v1.0.md, uploaded to the registered project and frozen with this registration. H1 (existence and prevalence; primary; directional; Theisen & Andow, 2025, Experiment 2). Among participants who, on their fulfilled-obligations/biased-evidence trial, (a) passed both manipulation checks under the original authors' criterion (responses strictly on the correct side of the scale midpoint for both checks), (b) rated the scenario above the scale midpoint on the plausibility check (> 50), and (c) gave a pre-information act-blameworthiness composite of at least 20, the proportion showing no meaningful reduction in act blameworthiness (change score > -5, using the original authors' own 5-point smallest meaningful blame reduction) is at least 10 per cent (the smallest prevalence of interest, SPI; provenance and justification in Preregistration Section 7.1).

H2 (discrete non-updating component; Theisen & Andow, 2025, Experiment 2). The between-person distribution of blame updating across the four moral-ignorance trials is better described by a latent-mixture model containing a near-zero updating class (model-implied mean change in the fulfilled/biased condition within [-5, +5]) than by a single-population linear mixed model with continuously distributed heterogeneity, under fixed model-selection rules (delta-BIC >= 6 AND parametric bootstrap LRT p < .01 with B = 500 AND smallest class >= 5 per cent AND no boundary solution). H2 does not establish psychological kinds by itself; it tests whether this dataset is better represented by a near-zero latent component than by continuous heterogeneity under severe preregistered rules.

No third confirmatory hypothesis is registered. An earlier internal draft carried a gated hypothesis for Landy and Perry (2024); reading their published Method before registration settled the gate negatively (no within-person updating structure, no mitigating information, no comprehension checks), so it was withdrawn before registration and before any data access.

S1 (secondary; dissociation-consistent subset). Among the H1 qualifying set, the proportion showing no meaningful blame reduction AND rating the agent's belief blameworthiness at or below the scale midpoint (composite <= 50) is at least 5 per cent.

S2 (secondary; comprehension-registration guard). The \"comprehension-intact\" qualifier attached to any H1 signal is retained only if non-updaters show no detectable registration deficit relative to updaters on the two manipulation checks, each expressed as condition-consistent registration strength (on the FB trial: obligations strength = raw obligations-check score; evidence strength = 100 minus raw evidence-check score). Conjunctive per check: (a) one-sided Welch deficit test non-significant at alpha = .05, and (b) observed standardised deficit < 0.4 pooled SD. If either check fails either condition, the qualifier is withdrawn and the H1 verdict is capped at \"non-updating present but not demonstrably comprehension-intact\". Full TOST equivalence tests (bounds +/- 0.4 SD) are additionally reported and, if passed on both checks, license the stronger wording \"statistically equivalent registration\".

**About the personal-information flags.** These are pattern matches, not confirmed disclosures, and they are tuned to over-report rather than miss something. Expect false positives:

- **Column names** are matched against identifying words in English and other European languages (`email`, `telefoonnummer`, `geboortedatum`, ...). A column called `phone_number` flags whether or not it holds one, and an empty or already-anonymised column flags on its name alone.
- **Values** are matched against the shape of an identifier. An IP address pattern also matches a version string or a dotted numeric code; a card-number pattern requires both a real issuer prefix and a checksum, but a long numeric ID can still coincide.
- **Free text** is flagged when a column holds long, mostly-distinct prose — the shape open-ended answers take. Most such columns contain no names at all.

A flag means *look at this column*. Where the data is already de-identified (an `ip` column reading `Anonymized`, a `name` column the authors emptied), no action is needed.

No file could be screened for careless responding.

**What this does not cover.** Only 0 of 86 data files could be screened: the rest had no detectable multi-item scale block, or too few respondents. Even in a screened file, these checks only look at multi-item rating scales — the only place where a repeated or flat answer pattern is interpretable. Single questions, open text, demographics and any item outside a detected scale block are never examined. A respondent can therefore answer most of a survey carelessly and still not be flagged here, and finding nothing is not evidence that a dataset is free of careless responding.

>              else if (ci$upper <  spi) "bound"

info.title: Understood but Unmoved: A Theory of Trait Judgmentalism and the Architecture of Evaluative Rigidity

text.text: This paper is the theory-stage statement of the Judgmentalism research programme and the direct companion to a peer-reviewed article now published as Boullineau, E. (2027), Moral violations are made, not found: A theory of motivated violation construction, New Ideas in Psychology, 84, 101313, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.newideapsych.2026.101313.
text.formatted: This paper is the theory-stage statement of the Judgmentalism research programme and the direct companion to a peer-reviewed article now published as Boullineau, E. (2027), Moral violations are made, not found: A theory of motivated violation construction, New Ideas in Psychology, 84, 101313, <ref type="url" target="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.newideapsych.2026.101313">https://doi.org/10.1016/j.newideapsych.2026.101313</ref>.

text.text: The published article points to a broader programme on evaluative rigidity, and the present paper supplies that stage.
This version supersedes Version 4 in full, under a new title, and has been submitted to Review of General Psychology.
A parent learns that their teenager stole from a shop.
The explanation arrives slowly and it is a good one, a friend in trouble, a debt collected by intimidation, a panicked attempt to help.
The parent listens, nods, repeats the explanation back accurately, agrees that it matters.
Then the verdict returns exactly where it began.
A thief is a thief.
Nothing in the exchange failed except the last step.
The context was heard, understood and accepted, and it weighed nothing.
The pattern has an audible signature.
It is the concession followed by the unmoved conclusion, the evaluator saying yes, I understand, but still.

Everyone recognises the person who produces it, because everyone knows a judgmental person, whether the colleague whose verdict on a co-worker survives every exonerating fact, the relative for whom one lapse settles a character permanently, or the online stranger for whom an apology is further evidence.
The word is ancient, the type is folkpsychologically vivid, and the construct, in this form, does not exist.

Psychology has measured judgmentalism at its edges, a religious judgmentalism scale (Beck & Miller, 2000), a measure of judgmental tendencies in first impressions (King & Pate, 2002), and a validated measure of judgmental communication about sex (Mutchler et al., 2022).
text.formatted: Psychology has measured judgmentalism at its edges, a religious judgmentalism scale <ref type="bibr" target="#b2">(Beck & Miller, 2000)</ref>, a measure of judgmental tendencies in first impressions <ref type="bibr" target="#b18">(King & Pate, 2002)</ref>, and a validated measure of judgmental communication about sex <ref type="bibr" target="#b27">(Mutchler et al., 2022)</ref>.

text.text: Each captures how readily a verdict is formed or how harshly it is voiced.
None measures whether a formed verdict on a person moves when comprehended mitigation arrives, and that is the construct this paper proposes.

Philosophy has begun to treat being judgmental as a vice of attention, in which a single act is made to epitomise the whole person (Dake, 2024; see also Vaccarezza & Zuolo, 2025, on judgmentalism as kin to moralism).
text.formatted: Philosophy has begun to treat being judgmental as a vice of attention, in which a single act is made to epitomise the whole person <ref type="bibr" target="#b8">(Dake, 2024</ref>; see also <ref type="bibr" target="#b39">Vaccarezza & Zuolo, 2025</ref>, on judgmentalism as kin to moralism).

text.text: An early philosophical treatment made judgmentalism an affective matter, a satisfaction taken in condemnation itself (Simon, 1989), and the construct proposed here is cognitive non-revision rather than satisfaction, a discriminant the measurement programme gets for free.
text.formatted: An early philosophical treatment made judgmentalism an affective matter, a satisfaction taken in condemnation itself <ref type="bibr" target="#b34">(Simon, 1989)</ref>, and the construct proposed here is cognitive non-revision rather than satisfaction, a discriminant the measurement programme gets for free.

text.text: Psychology, which owns the measurement problem, has measured the type's neighbours and stopped short of the revision step.
The omission is not an accident of fashion.
It follows from an assumption built into the paradigms that would otherwise have found the trait.

Studies of moral judgment, impression formation and blame present mitigating information, confirm that participants comprehended it, and read any subsequent movement, or its absence, as the evaluation's response to the evidence.
Comprehension is treated as entry.
If the evaluator understood the context, the context is assumed to have entered the evaluation, and a static verdict is read as the context having been weighed and found wanting.
This paper names that default the Revision Assumption.
The assumption is an inferential shortcut some designs permit rather than a doctrine the field defends, and it does its damage quietly, one unexamined verdict at a time.
Under it, the person who understands everything and revises nothing is invisible, because the measurement model has no category for them.
Their stillness is recorded as discernment.
This paper proposes the construct the Revision Assumption has hidden.
That construct, Trait Judgmentalism, is a stable individual difference in the effective weighting of comprehended mitigating information during the evaluation of persons.

Its defining mechanism, Contextual Moderation Failure, is a failure of post-comprehension weighting, in which the mitigation is perceived, comprehended, retained and accepted as true and relevant, and receives negligible weight in the revision of the verdict.
The trait is evaluative, not doxastic.

It concerns the evaluation of persons rather than the updating of beliefs in general, and its criterion is the global verdict on the person, not blame for the act, preferred punishment, or willingness to trust.
The missing construct is not a laboratory nicety.

A decade of work on moral outrage and polarisation indicates, as recent syntheses argue, that platforms amplify condemnation and that changing the supply of moral conflict changes attitudes downstream (Brady & Crockett, 2024; Piccardi et al., 2025).
text.formatted: A decade of work on moral outrage and polarisation indicates, as recent syntheses argue, that platforms amplify condemnation and that changing the supply of moral conflict changes attitudes downstream <ref type="bibr" target="#b5">(Brady & Crockett, 2024;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b29">Piccardi et al., 2025)</ref>.

text.text: That literature is situational and person-blind.
It explains when condemnation is amplified, and has no construct for who supplies the condemnation that will not retire when context arrives.
Organisational and machine-evaluation parallels follow in Section 8.
The contribution of this paper is a stage in person evaluation that current models do not formally address, and the individual difference that lives there.
The core claim can be put in one sentence.
For evaluators high in Trait Judgmentalism, relevant and credible mitigating context is comprehended and accepted but given negligible weight in revising the verdict on the person.
Section 2 shows that average evaluators do revise, and that the stages this claim separates are known to come apart.
Section 3 states the construct and its mechanism.
Section 4 situates the paper in its research programme.
Section 5 gives the architecture of evaluative rigidity that produces and expresses the trait, and names the Revision Assumption's measurement-side twin, the Expression Assumption.
Section 6 separates it from its neighbours.
Section 7 states the evidence position and the predictions.
Sections 8 to 10 draw out applications, limitations and the conclusion.
The baseline result in this territory is not controversial.

When people receive new information about a transgressor's mental states or circumstances, they update blame gradedly, systematically and roughly symmetrically, and they do so even under cognitive load (Monroe & Malle, 2019).
text.formatted: When people receive new information about a transgressor's mental states or circumstances, they update blame gradedly, systematically and roughly symmetrically, and they do so even under cognitive load <ref type="bibr" target="#b26">(Monroe & Malle, 2019)</ref>.

text.text: Beliefs about bad agents are, on average, held with more uncertainty and revised more readily than beliefs about good agents, a flexibility that has been linked computationally to forgiveness (Siegel et al., 2018).
text.formatted: Beliefs about bad agents are, on average, held with more uncertainty and revised more readily than beliefs about good agents, a flexibility that has been linked computationally to forgiveness <ref type="bibr" target="#b33">(Siegel et al., 2018)</ref>.

text.text: Impressions formed from strong negative behaviour can revise rapidly and durably when the new evidence is diagnostic or the original evidence is reinterpreted (Cone & Ferguson, 2015; Mann & Ferguson, 2015; Ferguson et al., 2019).
text.formatted: Impressions formed from strong negative behaviour can revise rapidly and durably when the new evidence is diagnostic or the original evidence is reinterpreted <ref type="bibr" target="#b6">(Cone & Ferguson, 2015;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b22">Mann & Ferguson, 2015;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b12">Ferguson et al., 2019)</ref>.

text.text: The average evaluator, in short, behaves roughly as the normative story requires.
The averages conceal two things.
The first is a domain effect, moral impressions being the place where revision is hardest.

Impressions grounded in moral stereotypes resist updating by individuating evidence more than those grounded in non-moral stereotypes (Rösler et al., 2025), moral traits dominate person perception (Goodwin et al., 2014), and negativity biases in moral impression updating are robust and motivationally sensitive (Yang et al., 2025).
text.formatted: Impressions grounded in moral stereotypes resist updating by individuating evidence more than those grounded in non-moral stereotypes <ref type="bibr" target="#b30">(Rösler et al., 2025)</ref>, moral traits dominate person perception <ref type="bibr" target="#b14">(Goodwin et al., 2014)</ref>, and negativity biases in moral impression updating are robust and motivationally sensitive <ref type="bibr" target="#b41">(Yang et al., 2025)</ref>.

text.text: The second is a residue inside the paradigms themselves.

In recent preregistered blame-updating experiments, substantial numbers of participants granted little exculpatory force to mitigation, and the paradigm cannot say whether comprehension or weighting failed (Theisen & Andow, 2026).
text.formatted: In recent preregistered blame-updating experiments, substantial numbers of participants granted little exculpatory force to mitigation, and the paradigm cannot say whether comprehension or weighting failed <ref type="bibr" target="#b37">(Theisen & Andow, 2026)</ref>.

text.text: Updating studies, meanwhile, report systematic departures from the Bayesian benchmark, with conservatism concentrating where priors are confident (Ba et al., 2024).
text.formatted: Updating studies, meanwhile, report systematic departures from the Bayesian benchmark, with conservatism concentrating where priors are confident <ref type="bibr" target="#b0">(Ba et al., 2024)</ref>.

text.text: The movers and the unmoved may be different populations hiding under one mean.
What no literature has yet asked is whether membership of the unmoved population is stable across occasions, general across targets, and specific to the evaluation of persons.
That is a trait question, and it has not been put.
A trait of non-revision is only coherent if comprehension and use can genuinely come apart, so the dissociation needs footing outside this framework.
It has several, and each carries a specific part of the load.
Knowledge neglect shows that people hold the relevant knowledge, can retrieve it on demand, and fail to apply it to the task in front of them even under adequate monitoring (Marsh & Umanath, 2014).
text.formatted: Knowledge neglect shows that people hold the relevant knowledge, can retrieve it on demand, and fail to apply it to the task in front of them even under adequate monitoring <ref type="bibr" target="#b23">(Marsh & Umanath, 2014)</ref>.

text.text: The dissociation it demonstrates is between possession and deployment.
The stored content is intact while the judgment proceeds as though it were absent.
For Trait Judgmentalism this licenses the core possibility, that an accepted representation can sit idle at the moment of use.

It does not license the trait itself, because knowledge neglect is documented as a general and largely situational phenomenon, and the claim that the idleness is stable, person-linked and specific to the evaluation of people goes well beyond it.

Good-enough comprehension shows that readers and listeners routinely form representations accurate enough to pass a check and then leave them unexploited by downstream judgment (Ferreira et al., 2002).
text.formatted: Good-enough comprehension shows that readers and listeners routinely form representations accurate enough to pass a check and then leave them unexploited by downstream judgment <ref type="bibr" target="#b13">(Ferreira et al., 2002)</ref>.

text.text: That dissociation sits between representation and use within a single act of understanding.
It licenses this paper's refusal to treat a passed comprehension check as evidence of weighting, and it says nothing about who leaves the representation unexploited, which is the trait question.
Perspective-taking research supplies three footings of its own.

Listeners who demonstrably register that a speaker's perspective differs from their own often fail to use it in referential communication, and use it more readily when prompted (Wang et al., 2020), which shows the comprehension-use gap narrowing under instruction and therefore not reducing to ability.
text.formatted: Listeners who demonstrably register that a speaker's perspective differs from their own often fail to use it in referential communication, and use it more readily when prompted <ref type="bibr" target="#b40">(Wang et al., 2020)</ref>, which shows the comprehension-use gap narrowing under instruction and therefore not reducing to ability.

text.text: Instructed perspectivetaking, meanwhile, fails to improve interpersonal accuracy across a large battery of tests (Eyal et al., 2018), and the finding matters here as a caution.
text.formatted: Instructed perspectivetaking, meanwhile, fails to improve interpersonal accuracy across a large battery of tests <ref type="bibr" target="#b11">(Eyal et al., 2018)</ref>, and the finding matters here as a caution.

text.text: An instruction to take a perspective is no guarantee of an accurate representation, which is why the mechanism of Section 3 verifies comprehension directly instead of inferring it from effort.

And trait empathy measures jointly explain roughly four per cent of the variance in everyday state perspective-taking (Depow & Inzlicht, 2026), which weakens, without eliminating, the rival on which the unmoved evaluator is simply low in trait perspective-taking, and supports the decision, made in Section 7, to measure the construct behaviourally rather than by inventory.
